PUBLIC COMMENT OF HELEN BRYANT

PUCT PROJECT NO. 58482

LARGE LOAD DEMAND MANAGEMENT SERVICE

PROPOSED NEW 16 TAC §25.521

To the Public Utility Commission of Texas

• Large loads should not be paid to reduce demand they voluntarily placed on the grid.

• Emergency demand reduction should be required through binding interconnection agreements.

• Large loads should pay the cost of their own curtailment equipment, testing, metering, and compliance.

• Residential customers and small businesses should not subsidize the program.

• Large customers that refuse or fail to curtail should face substantial penalties.

• Serious or repeated failure should result in suspension from the ERCOT grid.

• Companies should not be allowed to collect overlapping payments from multiple programs for the same reduction.

• ERCOT should independently verify actual performance.

• All payments, failures, penalties, waivers, and delivered megawatts should be publicly reported.

• A “critical load” exemption should require proof of a genuine public-health or public-safety need—not mere financial inconvenience.
